# knbsdata

<!-- badges: start -->
[![Lifecycle: experimental](https://img.shields.io/badge/lifecycle-experimental-orange.svg)](https://lifecycle.r-lib.org/articles/stages.html#experimental)
[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/Mustapha-Wasseja/knbsdata/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/Mustapha-Wasseja/knbsdata/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)
<!-- badges: end -->

`knbsdata` is an R client and standardisation layer for discovering,
downloading, documenting and analysing official statistics published by the
Kenya National Bureau of Statistics (KNBS).

The package aims to make it straightforward to find the right dataset,
understand its metadata and access conditions, retrieve it in a consistent tidy
shape, keep the provenance attached to the data, and cite it correctly.

## Scope of version 0.1.0

**This release covers survey and census study discovery, and nothing else.**

Implemented, against the Kenya National Data Archive: search studies, read their
full documentation, search their variables, and list their data files — with
provenance and citations attached throughout.

Not implemented:

- **Publications, aggregate indicators and geographic reference data.** All
  three live on `knbs.or.ke`, which returned `504 Gateway Time-out` throughout
  the source audit and every re-check over roughly six hours. Its endpoints were
  never verified, so no adapter was written rather than one being guessed at.
- **Microdata downloads.** The archive requires an account for every download.
  `knbs_download_microdata()` explains the official process and stops; the
  package does not automate sign-in or licence acceptance.
- **Documentation files.** The archive publishes no machine-readable listing of
  questionnaires or reports.

`vignette("source-status")` states all of this in full. Findings are in
[`dev/source-discovery/source-audit.md`](dev/source-discovery/source-audit.md).

## Installation

```{r, eval = FALSE}
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("Mustapha-Wasseja/knbsdata")
```

## What works today

```{r}
library(knbsdata)

# Which sources does the package know about, and how far are they verified?
knbs_sources()
```

```{r}
# Is anything answering? This form contacts nothing; knbs_status(live = TRUE) does.
knbs_status()[, c("source_id", "status", "message")]
```

Surveys (these contact the archive, so they are not run here):

```{r, eval = FALSE}
# Find a study
studies <- knbs_search_surveys("household budget")

# Read its documentation
meta <- knbs_survey_metadata("KEN-KNBS-KIHBS-2015-2016-v01")
knbs_cite(meta)

# Search its variables without downloading any microdata
knbs_variables("KEN-KNBS-KIHBS-2015-2016-v01", search = "expenditure")

# See what it holds, and on what terms
knbs_survey_files("KEN-KNBS-KIHBS-2015-2016-v01")
```

## What it will look like

These are specified but not yet implemented, and depend on sources that could
not be audited:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
knbs_search("consumer price index")
cpi <- knbs_get_indicator("CPI_ALL_ITEMS", start = "2020-01")
knbs_publications(topic = "economic survey", year = 2026)
```

## Access conditions

`knbsdata` will not circumvent registration requirements, licence agreements,
approval processes, authentication, rate limits or robots exclusions. Datasets
that require authorised access are represented in the catalogue with their
access conditions, but are not downloaded: the package points you at the
official access process instead.

Retrieved data and publications remain subject to KNBS terms and licences. The
MIT licence in this repository covers the software only.

## Sources change

Official portals are re-organised from time to time. When a source changes shape
the package should fail with a clear, classed error rather than return
incomplete data. If you hit one, please open a
[data source change issue](https://github.com/Mustapha-Wasseja/knbsdata/issues/new/choose).

## Contributing

See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md), including the checklist for adding a new
source adapter. Please note that this project is released with a
[Contributor Code of Conduct](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).

## Disclaimer

`knbsdata` is an independent open-source software project designed to facilitate
access to publicly available statistics and metadata published by the Kenya
National Bureau of Statistics. It is not an official KNBS product unless and
until KNBS formally adopts or endorses it. Users should consult the original
KNBS source for authoritative definitions, revisions, access conditions and
official releases.
